::: {#exm-batch-norm}

#### `nn.BatchNorm1d` on a minibatch

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
batch_norm = nn.BatchNorm1d(64)
pre = nn.Linear(64, 64)(x_train[:32]).detach()
normed = batch_norm(pre).detach()
print(pre.mean(dim=0)[:4], pre.std(dim=0, correction=0)[:4])
print(normed.mean(dim=0)[:4], normed.std(dim=0, correction=0)[:4])
largest_mean = normed.mean(dim=0).abs().max().item()
std_min = normed.std(dim=0, correction=0).min().item()
std_max = normed.std(dim=0, correction=0).max().item()
```

`nn.BatchNorm1d(64)` applies [batch normalization](#def-batch-norm) to 64 [pre-activation](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-pre-activation)s.
It starts with every $\gamma_j = 1$ and every $\beta_j = 0$ [@pytorch_batchnorm1d].
For 32 training images,
the first 4 pre-activations of a random layer have the means and standard deviations on the first line.
After batch normalization,
on the second line,
no column's mean is farther from 0 than `r sprintf("%.1e", py$largest_mean)`,
and the standard deviations run from `r sprintf("%.3f", py$std_min)` to `r sprintf("%.3f", py$std_max)`.

:::
